What could your future look like? Find out at our Open Events - bookings are now live! Are you already making music, performing, designing or creating? Or you're just starting to discover what you're interested in? Our Open Events are the perfect chance to see where The BRIT School could take you Discover the world-class creative training & academic curriculum you'll study for FREE Meet students and staff Explore our industry standard facilities Learn about the careers you can enter with the skills, qualifications and industry connections you'll build here Post-16 Open Event: Tuesday 29 September, 2 - 7:30pm Key Stage 4 Open Event: Thursday 15 October, 2 - 7:30pm Applications for our courses open on 1st September. Until then, book your Open Event place via the link in our bio See you there!
Take a quick survey to help shape the future of our campus https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/5VM95XF The BRIT School is imagining what's next for our campus - whether you're a student, member of staff, parent, alumnus or part of our wider BRIT community, we want you to help shape it. We're working with designers, architects and specialists to explore how our campus can better support everything we do - from learning and rehearsing to performing, collaborating and taking a break. Share your thoughts with us in our anonymous survey by clicking the link in our bio. Thanks in advance, and stay tuned for updates on how your ideas will shape our future!
Ahead of Moana arriving in cinemas on 10th July, director Thomas Kail joined students for a special Q&A. From bringing Hamilton and In the Heights to the stage to directing for the big screen, Thomas shared insights into his creative journey, the making of Moana, and the values that have shaped his career along the way. Hearing directly from world-class creatives helps our students see what's possible, while giving them the insight, confidence and inspiration to forge their own creative paths. A huge thank you to Walt Disney Studios UK for making it happen #moana

We're looking for a Teacher of Set Design to join The BRIT School. This is a fantastic opportunity for a creative and inspiring educator to help shape the next generation of theatre makers, designers and creative professionals in our Production Arts department. You'll teach students across model box construction, technical drawing, scenic painting, scenic design and CAD, supporting them from first ideas through to realised productions. For candidates with relevant experience, there may also be an opportunity to be considered for an Assistant Director role in Production Arts. Full time, permanent Closing date: 1 June 2026 Apply here: https://www.brit.school/vacancies Photo credit: @flavsfotografia
Last Saturday 28th March we launched a powerful new pilot programme called Connect To Inspire which aims to find, train and elevate the next generation of diverse dance talent in and around Croydon. This pilot programme is a new collaboration between The BRIT School, BRIT Kids, Rambert Company, Rambert School, Rambert Grades and the Croydon Schools' Dance Association, working together to strengthen dance pathways and create meaningful progression routes for the next generation. At The BRIT School, we believe talent should never be limited by access, and Connect To Inspire reflects our commitment to creativity, community and industry standard training. Rambert School graduates Luke Buckley and Jemima Sparrow have spent the last two months delivering 15 workshops in Croydon School. The workshops have introduced the Rambert Grades programme which will be delivered through Connect To Inspire to over 400 young people across Croydon. On Saturday, 30 young talented dancers attended Connect To Inspire's official Launch Event, where they; connected with one another, had a tour of The BRIT School facilities and learned more about this exciting new venture. This initiative places access, inclusion and opportunity at its heart, offering high quality dance training for young people across Croydon. We are grateful to Croydon Schools Dance Association, Rambert Grades and Rambert School for funding this project. Nicole Guarino and @jmaflickz
We were thrilled to welcome back #AlwaysBRIT Rrahiim Raphael, now a WME agent, who shared how he uplifts artists, helping them build their visual identity and cultural relevance through sponsorships, fashion campaigns and global brand partnerships. He encouraged students to connect with their peers, emphasising the power of the #AlwaysBRIT community within the creative industries and on the global stage. #WME #TheBRITSchool #BRITTransforms @poytonphotography

Peripatetic Music Lessons
Peripatetic Classes
The BRIT School provides facilities for students to enrol for private instrumental, voice, theory or technology lessons with highly skilled and industry experienced professional music teachers.
These lessons take place during the normal school day and a full course consists of 27 lessons. Some bursaries are available to assist with the cost.
Courses on offer:
Guitar electric/acoustic/classical
Bass guitar
Saxophone
Clarinet
Music Theory
Songwriting
Music Technology
Music Industry Mentoring

Anton Browne: Voice, Musicianship & Songwriting
About Anton
I am a singer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist, playing piano, guitar and bass. At The BRIT School, I teach voice, songwriting, practical musicianship, recording, and the keyboard, guitar and bass skills that support contemporary songwriters. My aim is simple: to help students develop the skills, confidence and creativity needed to bring their music to life.
Since The BRIT School opened in 1991, I have had the privilege of working with generations of talented young musicians. Alongside my work at BRIT, my experience includes:
Vocal Coach for the BBC's The Voice UK Series 1 Tour
Professor of Jazz Voice at Trinity Laban Conservatoire
Co-author of the original London College of Music (LCM) Popular Music Vocals graded syllabus
Teaching and workshop work for institutions including the University of Cambridge (APPS), ELAM, ACM, Goldsmiths and Roehampton University
Online reviewer and ambassador for Earthworks High Definition vocal microphones
In 2026, I introduced my AI Method for Musicians, incorporating creative tools such as Suno AI into classroom learning. Students explore how emerging technologies can support songwriting, arrangement and music production while maintaining their own artistic voice.
I particularly enjoy working with students who are interested in contemporary music styles and original creative work. While my specialism is not classical, opera or musical theatre, I am always happy to help students explore pop and contemporary vocal techniques alongside their existing studies.
One of the things I value most about The BRIT School is the opportunity to work with highly motivated and imaginative young artists. Our excellent facilities— including pianos, computers, recording equipment and professional audio technology—allow students to create, record and develop their music in a practical, industry-relevant environment. Alongside the school's resources, I bring a range of professional microphones, instruments and recording tools into lessons to enhance the learning experience.
What Students Can Expect
Lessons are tailored to individual goals, interests and experience levels. Areas we may explore include:
Understanding how the voice works and how to improve it safely Mapping, managing and extending your range
Developing vocal range, control and confidence
Breathing techniques and vocal efficiency
Effective practice strategies
Working with songs and finding the right key
Riffing, runs and improvisation
Scat singing and musical creativity
Microphone technique and recording skills
Songwriting and musical arrangement
Piano, guitar and bass skills for songwriters
Performance skills and artistic communication
Recording demo videos and developing online content
Collaborative music-making, jamming and creative exploration
Using AI tools creatively and responsibly within music production
Above all, I aim to create a supportive, enjoyable environment where students can develop their skills, discover their artistic identity and enjoy making music.

How to Apply & Admissions Policy
Applying to the BRIT School
We have two intakes:
You will need to apply for Key Stage 4 in September when you begin Year 9 in your current school. You will need to apply for Post 16 in September you begin Year 11 in your current school. Applicants who will be 18 at the start of the course cannot be considered. We do not admit students into Years 11 or 13. The BRIT School application process takes around 10 months.
Key Stage 4 (aged 14-16)
Post 16 (aged 16-18)
Click here to complete an application form.
If your application is successful
You will be invited to a practical workshop/audition. Please read the Admissions Policy carefully before making an application as this will explain the practical requirements and admission criteria.
Do I live close enough?
We accept students from most of Greater London and some parts of Kent and Surrey. Catchment postcodes: click here for a full list. We are allowed to take ten percent of applicants from outside this area, but only if you show unusual merit. We discourage long journeys so check the length of your commute from home to Selhurst station, situated five minute walk from the school. You will need proof of your address during the application procedure to show you are in the catchment area.
Do I have to pay?
It is free to attend The BRIT School. However, limits on the School’s budget mean that we do need to charge for certain activities, such as non-curriculum visits and peripatetic music tuition. In some subjects, students will also need to provide their own specialist professional equipment; each course’s individual documentation provides guidance.
Can I get financial support?
We have limited funds for bursary grants to support travel costs, free school meals and peripatetic lessons. This support is available where the main family income comes from Job Seeker’s Allowance, Income Support, Widowed Parent’s Allowance, Incapacity Benefit or a State Pension. We will also consider applications from students with a low family income. A copy of the Charging and Remissions Policy is available on request.
When will we find out?
Workshops will be held from December to March, and we will endeavour to communicate decisions within four weeks of your workshop/meeting date.
Can I apply if I have additional educational needs?
Our Additional Educational Needs (AEN) Department provides support for students with learning difficulties in order to help them overcome barriers to their learning and fulfil their potential.
The BRIT School welcomes applications from students with additional educational needs, in accordance with the School’s inclusion policy. However, you must still fulfil the criteria set out by the particular strand for which you would like to apply, such as passion and talent in your chosen area.
It is important that you let us know on your application form of any identified additional educational needs so that we can consider this throughout the admissions process and beyond. All applicants with an Educational Health Care Plan (EHCP) issued by their Local Authority will be supported in their interview by a member of our AEN Department.
If a student with additional educational needs is granted a place, the AEN Department will make contact prior to their admission in order to begin the process of working together with parents/carers and students. Some students are offered support within the classroom from one of our Learning Support Assistants (LSAs), while others spend time within the AEN Department’s facilities on an individual or group basis.
We also support teaching staff by providing them with relevant information and training.

Each site has its own collection of classes on offer, but all with the same ethos and high standards you would expect from The BRIT School. FAQs
How to book?
Select the course you wish to book and then click apply now.
Should I have any previous experience before applying and what age do you accept?
There are no requirements other than an interest and an open mind. Please note this is a full week program and connot be booked for single days. The ages are 7-18 years old.
What should we do for snacks and lunch?
Food and drink is NOT provided and students MUST bring a packed lunch/snack with them as well as a water bottle. There are water fountains on site and these will be able to be used. Please ensure that their packed lunches are NUT-FREE.
What is the daily timetable?
Children will arrive between 8.45am- 4pm and 9am Classes will start at 9am. Each lesson is 1 ½ hours long. For our younger students there will be break times at the end of each lesson. All students will have a one hour lunch break, in our canteen, or outside in our canteen area weather permitting. Pick up time is 4pm. Should you be required to drop off your child late or pick up early, this must be done by prior arrangement with the manager in person or via email.
What should I bring?
A healthy packed lunch (nut-free please) with 2 healthy snacks.
A water bottle — don’t worry if children drink it all, we have water fountains. Please no energy/fizzy drinks.
In warm weather a sun hat and suncream
Some might wish to bring a change of clothes, but this is not necessary.
You will not need to bring any specific equipment. This will be made available at the school.
What should I wear?
For the Performing Arts pathway, comfortable & suitable shoes for activities that they will be moving about in. Such as loose fitting clothing (e.g. a tracksuit, t-shirt, top). Ideally no jeans or skirts. Some sessions may require bare feet.
For the Creative Arts and Media pathway, this can be messy so comfortable clothing that is not special should they get paint or like on their clothing.
How can I let you know if my child has an AEN need or Medical condition?
When you complete the registration form you will be asked these questions. Please answer them fully and accurately so we can best accommodate your child.
Should your child require an Epi Pen or inhaler, they will need to show it to the manager at the beginning of each day that they have them on their person. This is for their safety.
What is BRIT Kids?
BRIT Kids is The BRIT School's Saturday programme that runs 36 Saturdays a year. Can't wait till October? No need. Join BRIT Kids Autumn term and enjoy a bit of BRIT every Saturday! Simply use the Apply link to join.
